task_instance: Wrote and executed a PostgreSQL cohort retention analysis query (the skill's 'Cohort Retention' pattern using DATE_TRUNC + CTEs + conditional COUNT DISTINCT) against a small sample users/user_activity dataset representing two monthly signup cohorts, then verified the month_0/month_1/month_3 retention counts by hand against the seeded activity rows.
evidence: Started local PostgreSQL 16 cluster (pg_ctlcluster 16 main start), created database 'skilltest'. Loaded schema.sql defining users(user_id, first_activity_date) and user_activity(user_id, activity_date) with 9 users across a Jan-2024 cohort (5 users) and Feb-2024 cohort (4 users), and 18 activity rows spanning several months. Ran cohort_retention.sql (adapted verbatim from the skill's Cohort Retention pattern, PostgreSQL dialect per the skill's Postgres reference section). Output: Jan-2024 cohort_size=5, month_0=5, month_1=3, month_3=2; Feb-2024 cohort_size=4, month_0=4, month_1=2, month_3=1. Manually cross-checked against the seeded rows (e.g. Jan cohort users 1,2,4 had Feb activity -> month_1=3; users 1,4 had April activity -> month_3=2; Feb cohort users 6,8 had March activity -> month_1=2; user 6 had May activity -> month_3=1) and all counts matched exactly, confirming the query is correct. Also ran EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the query successfully (from the skill's Postgres Performance tips section) to confirm it executes and profiles without error. Files produced in work directory: schema.sql, cohort_retention.sql, result.json.
